newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivian ex-ruler's first round vote win confirmed.
newsitem.headline: Bolivian ex-ruler's first round vote win confirmed.

text.p: Hugo Banzer, a general who led a 1971 coup and admits he acted in an "authoritarian way," will face Bolivan ruling party candidate Juan Carlos Duran in the final round of voting for president, unofficial results showed on Monday.

Legislators who meet in early August are theoretically free to pick either of the top two candidates, but since Banzer's party did better in legislative elections he is a virtually certain to return to power.

The complete count of Sunday's election confirmed projections showing Banzer of the Nationalist Democratic Action (ADN) in first place and Duran of the Nationalist Revolutionary Movement (MNR) second. Official results may take weeks to complete but the Fides-Bolivision count is usually highly accurate.

Banzer, now 71, seized pwoer in a 1971 coup and launched a drive against left-wing guerrillas. He does not deny his human rights record is not brilliant. "We acted in an authoritarian way, I admit," he said after voting ended. But he claimed he had no alternative because Bolivia, one of the poorest nations in Latin America, was going through a period of turmoil.

However, Banzer -- in his sixth attempt at the presidency since he was ousted himself in a 1978 coup -- has vowed that if Congress makes him president he will "respect the law and serve the Bolivian people."

Duran's party was shunned by many Bolivians unhappy with President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada's economic policies that many see as too hard on 70 percent of the population who live under the poverty line, analysts said.

Banzer endorses the free-market and privatisation drive highly praised by the international financial community but which appears to be testing the limits of Bolivians' patience. But, sensing the discontent with railways, telephones and services whose post-privatisation rates have shot up beyond the reach of many Bolivians, he promised to try to put an end to private firm monopolies and "humanize" the economy.
